claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be prepared as a simple, fully disordered FCC solid solution by high-temperature homogenization followed by rapid quenching.
The relatively low hardness and strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are caused by its fully disordered FCC solid-solution state.
The fully disordered state accounts for the alloy's relatively high plasticity and machinability.
Aging equimolar CoCrFeNiTi at 600 °C for up to 24 hours will induce short-range atomic order or nanoscale precipitates.
Rapid quenching will maintain a wholly disordered control state.
Nanoscale ordered domains or precipitates act as dislocation-pinning centers in CoCrFeNiTi.
Dislocations move relatively easily in the as-quenched disordered structure.
Easier dislocation motion produces lower hardness and strength together with higher plasticity and machinability.
Short-range order or nanoprecipitates formed during aging impede dislocation motion.
Greater impediment to dislocation motion increases hardness and yield strength while reducing ductility.
Aged samples will have significantly greater hardness than as-quenched samples.
Aged samples will have significantly greater yield strength than as-quenched samples.
Aged samples will have lower ductility than as-quenched samples.
If the aging-induced ordered domains or precipitates remain stable at 600 °C, the mechanical-property differences between aged and as-quenched samples will persist at that temperature.
If the aging-induced features dissolve at 600 °C, the mechanical behavior of aged and as-quenched samples may converge.
